scope.full_target:
Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

hypotheses.statement: u is jointly smooth on the open set ℝ^n×(0,∞).

binders.type: real scalar, existentially quantified at each point

hypotheses.statement: For every x∈ℝ^n and t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Δ_xu(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity of a selection of these scalars is assumed.

binders.type: compact subset of ℝ^n, existential after s,t

hypotheses.statement: For every pair of real times 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact set C⊂ℝ^n such that u(x,r)=q for every x∉C and every r∈[s,t].

source.statement: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n. The finite energy E:(0,∞)→ℝ is differentiable at every t>0 and E'(t)=0. In particular E(b)=E(a) for all a,b>0, with exactly the normalization E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n} (|u_t(x,t)|²+∑_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|²) dx and no assertion at time zero.

correspondence.explanation: The parameters n,m and H001 retain precisely the positive finite dimensions. Identify coordinate ℝ^n with Fin n → ℝ and target ℝ^m with EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); product-space and Euclidean domain norms are equivalent, so open sets, compactness, smoothness and coordinate derivatives agree, and volume on the coordinate product is precisely the specified product Lebesgue measure. A map on positive times admits an arbitrary total extension, and restriction of any such extension recovers the original map. H002 constrains smoothness only on the positive open domain; derivatives there depend only on the germ, so both extension and restriction preserve H002, H004 and pointwise H005. H003 is exactly the fixed unit vector condition, and H006 exactly requires one compact C for each closed positive time slab, with no extra scalar regularity in H005. Conversely the original data produce these hypotheses for every total extension. wDx evaluates the Fréchet derivative on the coordinate unit vector; wT, wLap and the squared Euclidean norms therefore give exactly the prescribed derivatives, componentwise Laplacian and Frobenius density. The conclusion quantifies over every positive real t, asserting Lebesgue integrability, ordinary differentiability and zero derivative of the actual integral, plus equality of energies at every two positive times. Restriction and extension give these conclusions in both directions because derivatives at positive times are local and the density sections and integrals coincide. No condition or assertion at time zero or outside positive times is imposed; the integral has no factor 1/2.
